title: US markets: the daily wrap
dek: How the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq opened and closed each trading day, the gap at the open, and the reasons reporters gave. Dates are US dates; the close comes at 2:30 am IST.
seoTitle: S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq today: open, close and gap, day by day
status: Stocks recover most of a steep early fall
bigLabel: S&P 500 close on Wednesday 25 Nov (US time)

glance.what: The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 on Wednesday 25 November, after being down as much as 3.2% during the day, as chip and AI shares fell again. The Nasdaq fell 0.62% and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Inflation data came in hot: the PCE price index rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier. On Monday the S&P 500 had jumped 4.73% after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
glance.why: Doubts about AI spending, new US tariff proposals and expectations of a Fed rate rise in December are weighing on tech shares. Big US moves often set the tone for Indian markets the next trading day.
glance.next: US markets are closed on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and have a half-day session on Friday, per Yahoo Finance.

forYou: Indian IT companies earn much of their money in the US, and foreign investors move money between the two markets, so a sharp Wall Street fall often shows up in Indian shares the next morning. This is information, not investment advice.
next: US markets are closed on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and reopen on Friday 27 November for a half-day session. Then the Fed's December meeting, where traders expect a rate rise.

events.title: Gap up and the S&P 500's best day since April
events.summary: The S&P 500 opened higher and rallied 2.35%, its best day since 8 April, as oil prices fell, CNBC reports via StockTitan. All 11 sectors rose. Nvidia fell about 4% after its board opened an investigation into reports about CEO Jensen Huang.
events.status: Market data · TheStreet, Zacks via Yahoo Finance

events.title: Gap down on hotter inflation; Nvidia falls 5%
events.summary: Stocks opened lower and closed down after October's core inflation rose 0.3%, more than forecast, CNBC reports, adding that expectations of a Federal Reserve rate rise next month grew. Technology was the weakest sector, and Nvidia ended down about 5%.

events.title: Gap up as CoreWeave's results revive the AI trade
events.summary: The S&P 500 opened higher and closed up 1.31% after cloud company CoreWeave beat forecasts and raised its outlook, which lifted chip and AI shares, CNBC reports. Every stock in the Philadelphia semiconductor index rose, per CappNotes. The S&P 500 ended within 2.6% of its record high, AP reports.

events.title: Gap down as Nvidia's CEO leaves and Iran tensions rise
events.summary: Wall Street opened lower and ended down 0.35% as Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO, rising tension with Iran and expectations of a Fed rate rise weighed on shares, Zacks reports via Yahoo Finance. Nineteen of the 30 Dow stocks fell.
events.status: Market data · Zacks via Yahoo Finance

events.title: Opens higher, then slips as chip stocks fall again
events.summary: Stocks opened higher but the S&P 500 closed down 0.40% as Nvidia and other chip shares fell after a hotter-than-expected inflation reading, Yahoo Finance reports. The Dow edged up 0.1%. All three indices still ended the week higher; the S&P 500 gained 2.5% for the week, AP reports.

events.title: Gap down and a 1.9% slide as chip stocks sell off before Nvidia's results
events.summary: The S&P 500 opened lower and fell 1.92%, its third straight loss, as chip and AI shares sold off, CNBC reports. Nvidia fell 4.1% a day before its earnings, after reports that its board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang. Only consumer staples and utilities rose, per CappNotes.

events.title: Fourth straight loss for the S&P 500 as software and health shares fall
events.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 and the Nasdaq had its fourth loss in a row, per Reuters and CappNotes. All 11 sectors fell. Software companies such as Salesforce and Intuit, and health insurers, fell most; Reuters also points to worries about AI spending, hints from Fed officials that a rate rise is possible, and higher import prices. October retail sales rose more than forecast. Nvidia fell 0.44% before its results, then rose after hours. The opening level could not be confirmed from two reports, so this day has no gap figure.
events.differs: 24/7 Wall St reports bigger falls: Dow −1.85% (955 points) and Nasdaq −0.91%. Reuters and CappNotes agree on the figures above.

events.title: S&P 500 slips for a fifth day; Dow falls 1.1%, Nasdaq rises
events.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth loss in a row, per Yahoo Finance and StockTitan. The Dow fell 561 points while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%. Health insurers fell after a US government proposal to step up anti-fraud checks on Medicare Advantage plans. Minutes of the Fed's last meeting showed nearly all officials expect further rate rises may be needed, per the Motley Fool. Nvidia fell 2.9% the day after its results. Amazon, an Anthropic investor, rose before Anthropic's share sale. The opening level could not be confirmed from two reports, so this day has no gap figure.
events.status: Market data · Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool
events.differs: Health insurer falls differ: the Motley Fool reports UnitedHealth −10.2% and Humana −13%; Yahoo Finance reported about 6% each during the day.

events.title: S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss; Dow drops about 1,100 points
events.summary: All three indexes opened higher and held gains through the morning, then turned lower, per 24/7 Wall St. The S&P 500 fell about 2% to about 7,177, its sixth loss in a row and its longest losing run since April 2024, per the Motley Fool. The Dow fell 2.19% and the Nasdaq 2.23%. Reporters linked the fall to talk of further Fed rate rises and worries about high share prices and inflation. Nvidia fell 3.3%. AMD fell 7.7% after a report alleged links to a blacklisted Chinese server maker, per the Motley Fool. Anthropic's shares started trading on the same day and closed 17.1% above their $83 IPO price. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure.
events.status: Market data · Motley Fool, 24/7 Wall St
events.differs: Closing figures differ slightly. The Motley Fool gives the S&P 500 at 7,177 (−2.00%), the Dow at 49,097 (−1,101 points, −2.19%) and the Nasdaq at 23,886 (−2.23%); 24/7 Wall St gives 7,177.55 (−1.99%), a 1,091-point Dow fall (−2.17%) and −2.00% for the Nasdaq. The two also differ on whether energy and consumer staples ended higher.

events.title: S&P 500 falls 3.7% for a seventh straight loss and enters a correction; Nasdaq turns negative for 2026
events.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39, its seventh loss in a row, per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes. It closed about 10.7% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October, which counts as a correction (a fall of 10% or more from a peak). The Dow fell 1.93% and also closed in a correction. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% and is now down for 2026. CappNotes puts the S&P 500's fall for the week at 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025. Reporters linked the fall to a sell-off in AI and chip shares and to expectations that the Fed will raise rates in December. Nvidia fell 14.01%; CappNotes cites a Reuters report that SEC enforcement staff are examining possible accounting issues at the company. AMD fell 13.25%. Anthropic fell 8.50% to $88.91 on its second day of trading, still above its $83 IPO price. Consumer staples was the only sector to rise, per CappNotes. Opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; Yahoo Finance reports the S&P 500 was down about 0.5% soon after the open.
events.differs: Yahoo Finance and CappNotes agree on the closing figures above, which imply a 19 November S&P 500 close of 7,175.83, slightly below the ≈ 7,177 recorded here. Yahoo Finance's article text also says 3.6% in one place. 24/7 Wall St gives bigger falls: S&P 500 −3.97%, Dow −2.11%, Nasdaq −5.57%. The VIX 'fear gauge' is given as 35.89 at the close by CappNotes and 38.40 by Yahoo Finance. For Anthropic, 24/7 Wall St gives a close of $88.30 rather than $88.91.

events.title: S&P 500 jumps 4.7% after Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang, ending a seven-day losing run
events.summary: The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, its best day since April 2025, per Investopedia (via Yahoo Finance). Its 327-point rise was its second-biggest ever in points. The Dow rose 3.01% to 49,595.31 and the Nasdaq 6.51% to 24,089.56. Before the open, Nvidia said its board had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Nvidia shares rose about 31%, their biggest one-day gain since 2003, and added about $950 billion in market value. Reporters also pointed to forced buying by traders who had bet on further falls, lower oil prices, and Oracle saying it has the funding it needs for its OpenAI computing deal. A Nomura strategist called it a "mechanical" bounce that does not settle worries about inflation, borrowing costs and AI spending. Anthropic shares fell on the day, by 1.43% per CNBC. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; the SPY fund that tracks the S&P 500 opened about 5% higher, per Yahoo Finance.
events.differs: ABC News gives the Dow's rise as 1,147 points; Investopedia and FinanceFeeds give 1,447.98, which matches the closing levels. Nvidia's close is $165.05 per FinanceFeeds and $165.36 per TASS citing Forbes.

events.title: Nasdaq falls 1.5% as the Nvidia rally fades; Dow rises 0.9% and closes above 50,000
events.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq 1.48% to 23,733.54, per AP (via La Nación) and BigGo Finance. The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. Chip and AI shares gave back part of Monday's rally. Nvidia fell 5.86% to $155.38, per Reuters data via MarketScreener, and the Philadelphia chip index fell 7.88%, per BigGo Finance. One analyst told Reuters that "one headline doesn't really resolve investor questions about the AI trade." Reports that the US may soon raise tariffs on China and other trading partners also weighed on shares, per TipRanks and Reuters. Retailers rose after strong results: Dollar Tree gained about 11%. A Conference Board survey showed consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November, above the 92.5 economists expected, which helped the Dow. Anthropic shares fell below their $83 IPO price; TipRanks puts the day's fall at 8%. Traders expect the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points in December, per the CME FedWatch tool. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; at 10:05 am the S&P 500 was down 0.5% after falling as much as 1.4%, per AP.
events.status: Market data · AP, BigGo Finance, Reuters
events.differs: Reuters' preliminary figures were slightly different: S&P 500 7,202.45 (−0.48%), Dow 50,028.79 (+433.48), Nasdaq 23,740.52 (−1.45%). Investrade gives the Dow's rise as 426.60 points and TipRanks as 398 points; the figures above match the closing levels. TipRanks puts Nvidia's fall at 8% rather than 5.86%.

events.title: S&P 500 ends 0.3% lower after a fall of as much as 3.2%; Dow edges up before Thanksgiving
events.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78, per AP and Yahoo Finance, after being down as much as 3.2% earlier in the day, per AP. The Nasdaq fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Stocks opened sharply lower as chip and AI shares sold off again: early on the Dow was down about 700 points, the S&P 500 2.1% and the Nasdaq 3.2%, per Yahoo Finance. They recovered most of the losses in the afternoon. Nvidia fell 3.91% to $149.30, per Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool, after falling as much as 8% during the day. The PCE price index, an inflation measure the Fed watches closely, rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, the highest since 2023, per Yahoo Finance. Core PCE, which leaves out food and energy, rose 3.3%, slightly above the 3.2% expected. Traders put the chance of a 0.25-point Fed rate rise in December at about 98%, per Yahoo Finance. The new US tariff proposals on 14 economies also weighed. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.82% as investors moved into bonds. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure. US markets are closed on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and reopen on Friday for a half-day session, per Yahoo Finance.
events.differs: AP rounds the S&P 500's fall to 0.3%; Yahoo Finance gives 0.25%. Yahoo Finance's summary bullets say the Dow rose 0.5% and the S&P 500 fell 0.2%, which do not match the closing levels it lists. Fox Business, writing during the session, reported Nvidia down 8.6%; the closing fall was 3.91%.
